references.text: The parallel account in the Gospel of Mark, where Jesus says that the poor widow gave more than all the others, because she gave all she had to live on ([ref:Mark 12:43-44|Markus 12:43-44]).

Paul describes how the churches in Macedonia, despite deep poverty, gave generously and beyond their means – the same principle Jesus highlights regarding the widow's gift ([ref:2 Cor 8:2-3|2. Korinterbrev 8:2-3]).

Paul emphasizes that a gift is judged by what one has, not by what one does not have – the same principle Jesus applies when he says the widow gave more than all others ([ref:2 Cor 8:12|2. Korinterbrev 8:12]).

Proverbs teach that little with fear of God is better than great wealth with turmoil – a wisdom principle that reflects Jesus' assessment of the widow's small gift as greater than the gifts of the rich ([ref:Prov 15:16|Ordspråkene 15:16]).

The Lord does not look at outward appearance, but on the heart – this principle underlies Jesus' evaluation of the widow's offering as more valuable than the gifts of the rich ([ref:1 Sam 16:7|1. Samuelsbok 16:7]).
God loves a cheerful giver – the widow's willing sacrifice of all she owned illustrates exactly this mindset ([ref:2 Cor 9:7|2. Korinterbrev 9:7]).
